description: Use on a flat PDF (one with no fillable fields: pdf_inspect lists none) before adding fields: it detects blanks that are drawn on the page as lines, boxes, underscores and checkboxes and returns a text or checkbox field for each, named from the nearest printed label, with a confidence from 0 to 1. Detect, review, then add and fill: look the list over (drop wrong ones, rename, adjust), pass the entries you keep to pdf_add_fields as fields (label and confidence may stay, they are ignored), then fill the result with pdf_fill. The same step in one call: pdf_add_fields with detect true. Each entry has type, name, page, x, y, width, height in PDF points from the bottom-left of the page as the viewer sees it, the frame pdf_add_fields and pdf_edit use. It does not find fields that are not drawn (a blank area with no line or box, a scanned image, shaded cells with no outline), and some detections are table cells or rules that are not blanks, so results are suggestions to review, not a guarantee. It finds blanks that are drawn as lines, boxes, underscores and checkboxes; it does not find a field that has nothing drawn. Review the result before relying on it. Pages are read with min_confidence (default 0.4, raise it to 0.6 for fewer but surer fields) and max_pages (default 40, at most 100). At most 200 fields per call, and a call stops at its time and work limit, so a large form can take several calls. While truncated is true: add the returned fields to the PDF (pdf_add_fields with fields), then call pdf_detect_fields on the resulting PDF with pages set to next_pages (exactly the pages not done, including a page cut at 200 fields; a sparse selection stays sparse); repeat until truncated is false. Sending the original PDF again repeats the same names and is not supported. pages_skipped lists pages not analysed: reason too_complex (more drawn shapes or text than the per-page limits; sending them again gives the same answer) or deadline (the call stopped first; they are in next_pages). Zero fields is a normal answer with a note. Read-only: the source is never modified.

max_pages.description: Analyse at most this many pages. Default 40.

min_confidence.description: Drop fields below this confidence. Default 0.4 (drops only the weakest candidates, such as unlabelled shapes); 0.6 gives slightly higher precision and about a quarter fewer checkboxes.

pages.description: Pages to analyse, 1-based: "1-3,5,8-". Default: all pages (up to max_pages).

password.description: Password to open the input, only needed for a user-password PDF (owner-locked files with an empty user password open without it).

pdf_path.description: PDF source: an https:// URL or a data:application/pdf;base64,… URI (this hosted server cannot read local file paths).

name: pdf_detect_fields

label.description: The printed label the name came from, empty if none

name.description: Taken from the nearest printed label; unique, no dot

x.description: Left edge in points from the page's left

y.description: Bottom edge in points from the page's bottom

next_page.description: First page not returned, or null when finished

next_pages.description: Page spec of exactly the pages not done (including a page cut at 200 fields), or null when finished

note.description: Present when no fields were found or pages were skipped

pages_skipped.description: Pages not analysed: too_complex (more drawn shapes or text than the per-page limits; sending them again gives the same answer) or deadline (the call stopped first; they are in next_pages)

truncated.description: The answer is incomplete (more pages than max_pages, more than 200 fields, or the call stopped at its limit): add the returned fields to the PDF, then send the resulting PDF again with pages set to next_pages; repeat until truncated is false

title: Detect fillable fields in a flat PDF
